findings.rationale: Previously, `GET /pulls/:id` attempted a live GitHub fetch on every call and fell back to persisted data only on failure. The new code serves only persisted data without any GitHub call. Any external caller that relied on the GET to trigger a refresh (e.g., to get the latest files/commits/body) will now receive stale data until they explicitly call `POST /pulls/:id/refresh`. The PR description frames this as intentional, but it narrows the contract for any deployed caller that is not updated in lockstep. The client in this diff is updated, but other consumers (e.g., CI runners, integrations) are not.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer refreshes data from GitHub
findings.rationale: Previously, `GET /pulls/:id` attempted to fetch the latest files, commits, and body from GitHub on every request (when a token was configured), persisting the result before returning. Now it serves only what is already stored in the database, with no network call. Any existing caller that relied on this side effect to get fresh data — such as an e2e test, CI runner, or external consumer — will now silently receive stale data without any error or indication that the data is stale. The caller keeps working (no crash), but the contract has narrowed: the implicit freshness guarantee is removed. The compatible alternative is to keep the old behavior as an opt-in (e.g., a query parameter `?refresh=true`) or to document the change prominently in a changelog so callers can migrate to calling `POST /pulls/:id/refresh` explicitly.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id response shape narrowed — extra GitHub fields removed
findings.rationale: The old success path returned `{ ...detail, id: pr.id }` where `detail` came from GitHub's `getPullRequest` and could include fields such as `labels`, `milestone`, `mergeable`, `mergeable_state`, `comments`, `review_comments`, etc. The new handler returns only the explicitly listed fields (id, number, title, author, branch, base, head_sha, additions, deletions, files_count, status, opened_at, updated_at, body, files, commits). Any caller that relied on those extra fields from `GET /pulls/:id` will now receive a narrower response. The new `POST /pulls/:id/refresh` endpoint still returns the full GitHub spread (`{ ...detail, id: pr.id }`), so callers can migrate to that endpoint if they need the extra fields.

Callers that relied on the implicit refresh to get up-to-date information will now receive stale data until they explicitly call `POST /pulls/:id/refresh`. The response schema is unchanged, so no caller breaks, but the behavior changes silently. The PR description states this is intentional and the client is updated with a Refresh button, but any external caller not updated will be surprised.

findings.title: New field `reviewUrl` uses camelCase, breaking the project's snake_case convention for JSON fields
findings.rationale: The stack context states JSON fields are snake_case. Existing fields in `PrMeta` (`cost_usd`, `latest_findings`) follow this convention. The new field `reviewUrl` is camelCase, which is inconsistent. While no existing caller depends on this field, the inconsistency will surprise developers and may cause issues if automated tooling (e.g., code generators, serialization libraries) expects snake_case. Rename to `review_url` to match the rest of the schema.
